title: Colors of the Lost Galaxy
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 4535, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Long spiral arms flecked with bluish color wind around a yellower central bulge in NGC 4535, a barred spiral about 50 million light-years from Earth in the constellation Virgo. Through a small telescope the galaxy looks faint and ghostly, which is why the amateur astronomer Leland S. Copeland nicknamed it the Lost Galaxy in the 1950s.

Hubble's sharp view shows how color can reveal a galaxy's stars. The blue tones scattered through the arms point to many young, hot stars. The yellow glow of the bulge suggests the center is home mostly to older, cooler stars.
Hubble observed the galaxy for the PHANGS survey, which aims to clarify how cold gas clouds and star formation relate to the shapes and other properties of galaxies.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed NGC 4535 through ultraviolet and visible-light filters from 275 nm to 814 nm. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet light is invisible to the eye, and through a small telescope this galaxy looks hazy and ghostly rather than detailed and colored.

explore: The PHANGS-HST Collection had its first public release on 11 January 2021. The Hubble observations of NGC 4535 used Wide Field Camera 3 with filters running from the ultraviolet through visible light.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with long arms dotted with blue patches around a yellowish central bulge.
